sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in route tools, validation helpers, the user lookup, the notification service and database access.
sections.why: Needed to receive requests and save or read notifications.

sections.name: RegisterDeviceDto
sections.title: Device token input
sections.what: Describes the data a phone sends to register itself: a required push token, a required device type and an optional device name.
sections.why: Keeps invalid registrations from reaching the database.
sections.watch_out: This class is defined in this file rather than in the shared input file, so it is easy to miss when changing input rules.

sections.name: NotificationController
sections.title: Notification routes
sections.what: Provides routes to register a device, unregister a device by token, list the latest 50 notifications, mark all as read and mark one as read.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond covering the phone and in-app history needs.
sections.watch_out: Mark-all-read and mark-one-read use the user id filter, but unregister does not, so it is the odd one out.

summary: Provides routes to register or remove a phone's push token, list notification history, and mark notifications as read.
purpose: Connects the mobile app to the push notification system and shows the user their notifications.
why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the usual pattern of one route per action.
how: Register saves a device token for the user. Unregister marks a token inactive by its value. History returns the latest 50 notifications. Read-all and read-one mark notifications as read for the user.
inputs: Device token details from the request body, the token or notification id from the URL, and the user id from the token.
outputs: Database results for each action, returned directly to the caller.
risks: The unregister route does not check that the token belongs to the signed-in user, so anyone who knows a token can deactivate it.
debug: If pushes stop, check that the device is registered and active. If a notification shows as unread, check its user id and read time.
